summary: Large fintech using LLMs for realtime support and transaction summarization. Engaged for evaluation of hosted API vs dedicated GPU pool. Initial POC showed quality OK but projected per-token and GPU run costs exceed their internal target; procurement froze. Primary loss vector: unit economics (token/GPU cost + commit size) do not meet finance constraints.
notes:
Lead: CTO Mark Villar (finance-driven). Champion left during Dec reorg — contact is now Head of Data (interim).
- Use case: real-time chat for customer support + embeddings for instant account lookup; 99th-pctl latency target ~120ms on average conversation turn; throughput target ~600 concurrent sessions.
- Cost sensitivity: finance insists on <$70k committed annual spend or clearly < $0.04 / 1k tokens equivalent; conservative forecast requires unit cost < competitor offer.
- Model preference: prefer open models (Llama/Redwood-curated) but will accept smaller proprietary variants if TCO improves. Routing/fallback: need low-cost fallback for peak hours and regional routing (NA + EU).
- Security: SOC2 + SSO/SAML + audit logs mandatory; preference for VPC/private control plane for production.
- Procurement: legal requested full security pack and on-prem evaluation; on-prem evaluation would increase TCO by ~25% vs hosted — cause for pushback from finance.
- Direct quote (CTO): "We like the latency, but the numbers don't close unless we can get the committed GPU economics closer to what NimbusAI put on the table."
- Alternative considered: NimbusAI offered 18-month reserved GPU pool at lower effective token rate (but longer commit). Axiom Bridge rejected long-tail commit length.
- Internal politics: product champion promoted out of role in Dec; no clear exec sponsor to sign larger commit.
- Next actions previously agreed: SE to return with quantified quantization/PRQ scenario and three-year blended TCO by 2026-03-01; AE to reconvene with procurement Q2 post-budget refresh.
